items.detail: Thursday turned a one-day bounce into the best session in a month — the **S&P 500 rose 1.06% to 7,747.71**, the **Dow added 624.16 points (1.18%) to 53,686.11** and the **Nasdaq jumped about 1.4%**, a second straight advance that more than doubled Wednesday's gain.
items.why: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he is willing to support holding the policy rate steady if inflation keeps progressing toward 2%, adding a second and more senior dovish voice to Williams' pushback and collapsing the September hike premium that had defined the prior week.

items.detail: Waller moved the September decision onto a single data point, saying his vote will be **"heavily influenced" by the August CPI report due September 11** — "if inflation comes in hot, I would consider a rate hike" — and **CME FedWatch odds of a September hike fell to 50.4% from 63.2%** in a day.
items.why: Waller is a sitting governor rather than a regional president, so his conditional framing converted what markets had priced as a near-certain hike into a coin flip that now hinges entirely on next week's inflation print.

items.detail: The bond market did the repricing the equity rally was built on — the **10-year yield fell to 4.78%**, the **2-year dropped as much as seven basis points to 4.30%** and the **dollar index slipped 0.13% to 99.545**, with the whole curve down three to five basis points.
items.why: The front end carries the most direct exposure to a September policy move, so Waller's willingness to hold rates was expressed first and hardest in two-year yields and then transmitted into a weaker dollar.

items.detail: The activity data came in hot even as the labour data stayed soft — **ISM Services printed 55.4 against a 54.1 consensus**, up 1.3 points from July, with the **new orders index at 60.9, a three-and-a-half-year high**, while **jobless claims rose to 206,000** from 204,000.
items.why: A services economy accelerating into an oil shock is exactly the combination that would validate a hike, which is why the strong ISM did not stop the rally but did make Waller's CPI condition the market's whole focus.

items.detail: Broadcom delivered the quarter and the stock still went nowhere — **revenue rose 86% to a record $29.6 billion**, adjusted **EPS jumped 96% to $3.32** and **AI semiconductor revenue soared 221% to $16.7 billion**, but **Q4 guidance of $34.8 billion came in under the $35.03 billion consensus** and shares fell in extended trade.
items.why: The beat was only 0.53% on revenue against expectations that now assume near-perfect AI execution, so a guidance figure a fraction below consensus was enough to leave the ninth straight quarterly beat unrewarded.

items.detail: Crude spiked to a fresh high before fading again — **Brent reached $99.38 a barrel by 8am ET, up $3.27 from the prior morning**, then settled back to about **$95.25 (-0.40%)**, while **gold rose 1.39% to $4,385** for a second day of gains.
items.why: Iran's Revolutionary Guard retaliated against US positions in Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Iraq and the UAE, briefly pushing Brent toward triple digits, but the absence of any actual disruption to Hormuz flows let the risk premium bleed out again by the close.

items.detail: Thursday's early rebound completely unwound into a fourth straight loss — the **Nifty 50 opened at 23,997.95, hit 24,025.40 intraday, then closed at its low of 23,873.45, down 41 points (0.17%)**, with the **Sensex off 417.49 points (0.55%) to 76,152.86** after selling intensified in the final hour.
items.why: Brent's push back toward $99 during Indian hours erased the de-escalation trade that had gapped the index above 24,000 at the open, and gains in banking and realty were not enough to offset renewed selling in IT, FMCG and autos.

items.detail: Friday opened with the strongest gap of the week — **GIFT Nifty rose 133 points to 24,065.50**, the **Sensex opened up 504.16 points (0.66%) at 76,657.02** and the **Nifty added 37.45 points to 23,910.90**, with **Bajaj Finserv leading at +2.56%** alongside HCL Tech, UltraTech Cement, Maruti and Asian Paints, and Eternal the only Sensex loser.
items.why: Waller's willingness to hold US rates steady sent Wall Street to its best session in a month and pulled Treasury yields and the dollar lower overnight, which is the cleanest possible setup for emerging-market risk appetite at the Indian open.

items.detail: The institutional picture flipped on Thursday — **FIIs turned net sellers of ₹2,345.87 crore** after buying into the earlier decline, while **DIIs stepped up sharply to buy ₹4,977.46 crore**, more than double their prior-session purchase.
items.why: Foreign allocators cut Indian exposure as the rupee and the import bill absorbed a fourth day of elevated crude, while domestic institutions used the weakness to deploy steady SIP inflows, so the selling was absorbed rather than amplified.

items.detail: Breadth swung back hard at Friday's open, with **1,843 advancers against 774 decliners** on the NSE — a near 2.4-to-1 ratio after four sessions in which the tape had been dominated by decliners.
items.why: A broad-based advance rather than a narrow, index-heavyweight move signals the buying is coming from re-risking across mid and small caps once the global rate scare receded, not just from a few large-cap flows.

items.detail: The oil-to-currency channel remains the binding constraint — the **rupee is holding near ₹94.94 to the dollar** with **Brent still above $92**, and India imports roughly **85% of its crude requirement**, feeding straight into fuel, freight, fertiliser and food prices.
items.why: Every dollar on the barrel widens the current account and pressures the rupee, which imports inflation back into the domestic basket and narrows the RBI's room to support growth — the reason four sessions of crude strength outweighed a 7.8% GDP print.

items.detail: Bitcoin staged the biggest single-day repricing of the cycle so far, breaking back above $80,000 and **reaching $82,200 — its highest level since May** — after spending Wednesday trading near $77,200, and dragging the whole complex up with it.
items.why: Waller's signal that he could support holding rates flipped the dollar and Treasury yields lower simultaneously, and Bitcoin is the highest-beta expression of the September hike trade that had been suppressing the market all week.

items.detail: The move was a full-scale short squeeze, not accumulation — **more than $500 million of crypto liquidations in 24 hours**, with **over $415 million of that on the short side** and roughly **$250 million in Bitcoin contracts alone**, a five-fold escalation from the $82 million squeeze a day earlier.
items.why: Traders had built and then rebuilt short positions into what still looked like a probable September hike, so a second dovish Fed headline in two days forced a cascade of buy-backs that mechanically accelerated the rally as it went.

items.detail: The event that decides the next leg has shifted — **September hike odds dropped to 50.4% from 63.2%** on CME FedWatch, meaning the market that priced a 66% hike probability two days ago is now a coin flip ahead of the **FOMC on September 15-16**.
items.why: Waller made his own vote explicitly conditional on the August CPI report, so the pricing moved from a Fed reaction function traders thought they understood to a single unknown data point, and the implied probability collapsed to the midpoint.

items.detail: The ETF rotation reversed direction outright — **spot Bitcoin funds took in $101 million** led by **BlackRock's IBIT at $115.4 million** against **$56.2 million out of Grayscale's GBTC**, while **Ether ETFs posted a $48.2 million net outflow** that ends the eleven-day inflow streak, with **ETHA -$53.4 million**, **FETH -$26.2 million** and **ETHE -$23.5 million**.
items.why: The rotation out of Bitcoin products and into ETH, SOL and XRP vehicles that ran through August has flipped as allocators move back up the quality curve into the largest, most liquid vehicle ahead of a binary Fed meeting.

items.detail: The altcoin ETF channel turned negative alongside Ether — **XRP and Solana funds joined ETH in daily outflows** in the same session Bitcoin products drew in over $100 million, even though **Solana ETFs remain the standout of 2026 with cumulative inflows above $1.4 billion** and 33% growth on the year.
items.why: The altcoin vehicles are funded by a much thinner and more tactical allocator base than IBIT, so they are the first to see redemptions when the marginal buyer de-risks, regardless of the structural inflow trend still intact underneath.

items.detail: Two prints now stand between here and the FOMC — **August non-farm payrolls at 8:30am ET today**, with consensus around **53,000 jobs** and unemployment at **4.1%**, followed by the **August CPI report on September 11** that Waller named as the decision input; traders flag **$76,200-$76,500** as Bitcoin's support and **$77,700-$78,300** as near-term resistance.

crossCuttingTheme: A single Fed governor reset every market on the same axis: Waller's statement that he is willing to hold rates if inflation keeps improving cut September hike odds from 63.2% to 50.4%, pulled the 2-year yield to 4.30% and the dollar to 99.545, and that one move in the front end lifted the S&P 500 1.06% to 7,747.71, sent gold up 1.39% to $4,385, squeezed over $415 million of crypto shorts as Bitcoin hit $82,200, and gapped the Sensex 504 points higher at Friday's open — but because Waller tied his own vote to the August CPI report on September 11, the entire repricing is now conditional on an inflation print that has not happened yet, with today's payrolls the first test.
